title: One-shot Routing in Quantum Networks
authors: Nadav Lavi, Nir Gutman, Ido Kaminer, Ariel Orda
abstract: Distributed quantum computation requires many entangled pairs to be available simultaneously, so routing must optimize fidelity from a fixed, short-lived set of network resources rather than the rate of pairs accumulated over time. We formulate this one-shot routing problem for heterogeneous Werner-state links and jointly optimize path selection and the schedule of entanglement swapping and distillation. We show that the common purify-then-swap ordering is not optimal network-wide and that exact schedule enumeration requires $m^{Θ(m)}$ time. We introduce Fidelity-Optimizing Local Detours (FOLD), a heuristic that starts from the highest-fidelity path and merges a detour only when distillation improves on both routes and raises end-to-end fidelity. FOLD runs in polynomial time, recovers almost all of the optimal fidelity on tractable instances, and is four orders of magnitude faster than exact optimization at circuit rank $5$. On the Internet topologies where any strategy improves on shortest-path routing, FOLD achieves the highest mean end-to-end fidelity among the polynomial baselines. We further extend the formulation to links whose fidelities are known only as distributions, where uncertainty, rather than the effort spent routing, limits the fidelity delivered. Through an example of requests competing for the same links, we show that coordination becomes a condition for feasibility, and that a shared path budget controls the fidelity trade-off between them.
summary: This paper tackles the challenging one-shot routing problem in quantum networks, where the goal is maximizing connection fidelity from finite resources. The authors develop the FOLD heuristic, a polynomial-time algorithm that efficiently finds near-optimal routing schedules by intelligently interleaving entanglement swapping and distillation. This work is vital for designing scalable quantum communication protocols.
main_problem: The paper addresses the complex 'one-shot routing' problem in quantum networks, which requires optimizing end-to-end fidelity from a fixed, limited set of entangled resources rather than maximizing the rate of resource generation.
main_result: The proposed heuristic, FOLD, runs in polynomial time and achieves near-optimal end-to-end fidelity, significantly outperforming exact scheduling methods whose complexity is super-exponential.
method: The authors introduce the Fidelity-Optimizing Local Detours (FOLD) heuristic, which iteratively improves paths by merging detours only when distillation boosts the overall fidelity on both branches.
model_or_system: The model is a quantum network connecting nodes via links characterized by Werner-state entangled pairs. The process involves jointly optimizing path selection, entanglement swapping, and distillation schedules.
key_observables: End-to-end fidelity ($F = \langle\Psi^-|ho|\Psi^-angle$), which quantifies the quality of the quantum connection.
important_parameters: The size of the network (number of nodes $n$ and edges $m$), the circuit rank $r(G)$, and the path budget $k$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to evaluate fidelity for swapping and distillation operations, and the heuristic relies on bounding the number of successful merges by the graph's cycle rank.
figures_summary: Figures compare fidelity achieved by various scheduling strategies (e.g., purify-then-swap vs. optimal interleaving) and demonstrate the polynomial scaling of the FOLD heuristic compared to exponential exact solvers.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the one-shot routing formulation, contrasts it with rate-based models, develops the mathematical framework for fidelity calculation, introduces the intractable exact solution, and finally proposes and analyzes the polynomial-time FOLD heuristic.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, computationally tractable algorithm (FOLD) for optimizing resource utilization in quantum communication networks, which is crucial for scaling up quantum internet infrastructure.

Fidelity of all 2,885 operation sequences connecting A and B on the graph shown. Each marked strategy below is drawn as purify (P) and swap (S) operations, the edges an operation consumes colored and any unspent edge left pale. The strategies are purify-then-swap (PtS), swap-then-purify (StP), the recursive purify-and-swap reduction (Recursive, Section 3.4) [36] and FOLD, which leads all three. PtS, the ordering most schedulers assume, is the weakest here.
